---
name: reduction-needs-its-converse
description: Restating a walled obligation is only a reduction if you also prove the converse; the affine Sym^n case fell out for free once the interface was identified with a colimit.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a blocked obligation gets restated in a cheaper-looking form, **prove the converse
before calling it a reduction**. The new form must be *equivalent* to what the consumer
needs, not merely sufficient — otherwise you have relocated the debt, possibly upward, and
the green build cannot tell you which.

Concretely (AJC, `ajc-albanese`, 2026-07-28): `SymPowData C n` for `n ≥ 2` was priced at
2400–3800 lines as "construct `Sym^n C` as a scheme quotient by a finite group action,
affine-and-glue". Two sessions declined it as a subproject, correctly *at that statement*.
The object is in fact a **colimit of the `S_n`-action on `C^n`**, and once stated that way:

- the symmetry hypothesis (`hproj`), which had only an `n = 1` witness, became `colimit.w`
  — free at every `n`;
- the **affine** case came out proved at every `n` from mathlib's colimits alone, with the
  carrier identifiable as `Spec` of the invariant subring (limits in `CommRingCat` are
  computed as sections, and a one-object diagram's sections are its fixed points);
- the over-category layer vanished: `Over.forget` *creates* colimits, so the residue is a
  statement about `Scheme` with no base and no curve in it.

`hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` — the converse direction — is what makes this honest: nobody
can supply the interface without supplying the colimit.

**Why:** four lanes independently found "the frontier is an artefact of how strongly the
obligation was stated" on one day, which is exactly when a real pattern becomes a reflex
applied without a brake. The brake has two parts. First (from `ajc-fbc`): try the weaker
statement the consumer actually instantiates, read the leftover goal, and *believe it* —
sometimes the wall is real, as their Čech naturality squares were. Second (this item):
prove the converse, or you cannot distinguish a reduction from a relocation.

**How to apply:** before budgeting a "missing construction", ask what the consumer uses the
object *through* — if only a universal property, name that property categorically and check
whether mathlib already has the relevant (co)limits. Then prove both directions. Related:
[[isolating-a-residue-as-a-class]], [[sym-g-as-interface-not-sorry]],
[[search-object-shape-not-argument-shape]], [[port-the-idea-not-the-proof]].
